audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads HARD while tone is the even yellow, diffRating is 5.5/10 and both breakdown.difficulty and the final rating say 'Even matchup'. Separately the early text and whys[0] credit his sustain to 'his Q (Drunken Rage pool)'.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is Q and Drunken Rage is W — two different slots merged into one wrong name. His actual sustain is Happy Hour (P), which heals him every time he uses a skill; Drunken Rage is the damage-reduction and auto-empower button. Calling it 'his Q pool' sends you to the wrong tell.
audit.corrected: diff set to EVEN to match every other grade on the page, and the sustain re-attributed to Happy Hour with Drunken Rage named as the W damage-reduction window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named the clock on six different lines and never once given a number, so every "punish the cooldown" instruction is unactionable.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6s, Drunken Rage a flat 5s and Explosive Cask 100/85/70s, against your Miasma at 24s. A 14s Body Slam versus a 24s Miasma means you cannot ground every slam — that gap is the real lane.
audit.corrected: 14s, 10s, 5s and 100s written into the cooldown block, the trigger line, the all-in window and the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells you what Drunken Rage actually does before it hits, and the Happy Hour heal is never named, so no anti-heal timing appears anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's Drunken Rage text: 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing, he becomes boisterous and belligerent, dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received.' The one-second drink is a visible wind-up and an auto-attack reset — that is your cue to back off, not the slam. And Happy Hour heals him on every skill cast, which is what erodes your poison chip over a long lane.
audit.corrected: The one-second drink named as the tell, the reset stated, Happy Hour named as the sustain, and Grievous Wounds timing added.

edits.before: At level 1 you have one ability and no poison to stack, and his Q pool sustains your single poke — neither side wins, so just last-hit.
edits.after: At level 1 you have one ability and no poison to stack, and Happy Hour heals him off every cast — neither side wins, so just last-hit.

edits.before: Sustain on his Q pool through your poke and force a short brawl where his W reduction beats your DPS before E gets rolling
edits.after: Sustain on Happy Hour through your poke and force a short brawl where Drunken Rage's reduction beats your DPS before E gets rolling

edits.before: Body Slam (E) into you, land Barrel (Q) for the slow, and pop W to tank your Twin Fangs through the burst
edits.after: Body Slam (E, 14s) into you, land Barrel Roll (Q) for the slow, and drink Drunken Rage to tank your Twin Fangs

edits.before: Level 1 is even — you have a single ability and no poison stacking, and his Q (Drunken Rage pool) sustains whatever lone poke you land, so just last-hit with the tip of Noxious Blast. Once you hit 2 and especially 3 you take over: prime with Q, then chain Twin Fang (E) on the poisoned target — each E refunds cooldown and mana while the poison ticks, so you out-DPS him before his W damage reduction matters. Bait his Body Slam (E) and use Miasma (W) to ground his follow-up — note the grounding denies his NEXT dash, it won't cancel a slam already mid-flight — and dodge his Barrel so he never gets the slow to walk you down.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — you have a single ability and no poison stacking, and Happy Hour heals him off every skill he casts, so just last-hit with the tip of Noxious Blast. Once you hit 2 and especially 3 you take over: prime with Q, then chain Twin Fang (E) on the poisoned target — each E refunds cooldown and mana while the poison ticks, so you out-DPS him before Drunken Rage matters. His one-second drink is the tell, not the slam: when he starts sampling, step back, because the empowered auto is a reset. Bait Body Slam (E, 14s) and Miasma the follow-up — grounding denies his NEXT dash, not one mid-flight.

edits.before: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E your Twin Fangs chain near-continuously, and Serpentine Grace (no boots, escalating move speed) plus Q's speed buff let you kite his Body Slam → Barrel → W combo while you shred him. When he commits his slam, drop Miasma (W) where it grounds his escape and answer with E spam; at 6, face him and hold Petrifying Gaze for his all-in — he dives with the slam, you R him point-blank and the stun turns a won trade into a kill. The one thing that flips a trade is his Explosive Cask: never brawl with your back toward his side, or the knockback punts you to his tower or jungler.
edits.after: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E your Twin Fangs chain near-continuously, and Serpentine Grace plus Q's speed buff let you kite his Body Slam into Barrel Roll while you shred him. His 14s slam outpaces your 24s Miasma, so ground the recommit rather than the entry, and treat the one-second Drunken Rage drink as your cue to step out of the empowered auto. At 6, face him and hold Petrifying Gaze for the all-in — he dives with the slam, you R point-blank and the stun turns a won trade into a kill. Never brawl with your back to his side or Explosive Cask punts you home.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze answers his all-in: when he Body Slams in, face him and R to stun him point-blank, then chain E to convert the won trade into a kill before his W expires.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze answers his all-in: when he Body Slams in, face him and R to stun him point-blank, then chain E — his slam is 14s and Happy Hour will not out-heal that.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. It governs your forward steps. - W Miasma spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: 14s at rank 1 — engage and escape in one button, and your Miasma is 24s, so you cannot ground every one. - Barrel Roll: 10s. - Drunken Rage: 5s, a one-second drink and an auto reset. - Explosive Cask: 100s.

edits.before: Track Gragas’s Body Slam: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s against your 24s Miasma, so ground the recommit, not the entry. The one-second Drunken Rage drink is the burst tell.

edits.before: Commit on Body Slam’s cooldown, on your Seraph's / Liandry's spike, and with your jungler’s setup. His answer goes first; yours goes last.
edits.after: Commit inside Body Slam's 14s downtime, on your Seraph's / Liandry's spike, and with your jungler's setup. Never into the drink animation.

edits.after: - Cassiopeia vs Gragas - Body Slam is 14s, Miasma 24s. - Ground the recommit, not the entry. - The one-second drink is the tell. - Grievous Wounds beats Happy Hour.

edits.before: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Engage and escape in one 14s button, and your Miasma is 24s — pick which slam you ground, and ground the recommit.

notes: Explosive Cask knocks you back and you have no dash, but whether the displacement can pull you out of your own Petrifying Gaze cast is not in any local file, so I left that unstated. Also unverified: whether Miasma's grounding can stop a Body Slam already in flight — the page's existing 'denies his NEXT dash' caveat is the safe read and I kept it. Twin Fang's derived 'projectile' flag contradicts its targeted description and nothing here relies on it.
